title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Uganda, the ICSP programme helped families strengthen their livelihoods and improve food security through the S4Nut approach, which supports climate‑smart farming and better nutrition. Many households reported stronger incomes, with 45% earning more than before, and most people now able to save or borrow through community financial groups (83% informal and 46% formal access). Families adopted improved farming practices (60%) and saw better diets, with 85% achieving acceptable food consumption and 65% of children eating more diverse meals. Private‑sector partners, like Harvest Thrive, helped farmers access quality seeds, skills and markets to build long‑term resilience.. ICSP strengthens household food and nutrition security by supporting nutrition‑sensitive practices, kitchen‑garden production and positive behaviour change, which is essential in Uganda where seasonal shortages, climate pressures and limited dietary diversity continue to put vulnerable families at risk.
